A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MTJD/MTAD research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, pseudocode, and Appendices A–G support comparison, including matching material relocated in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original decoding experiments, downstream evaluations, energy measurements, and ablations using GPT-3.5, Llama-2, and OPT models.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Llama-3 evaluations, HumanEval results, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The MTJD formulation and MTAD procedure remain unchanged: auxiliary beam sampling, joint-likelihood verification, acceptance of the longest qualifying prefix, and an additional target-model token. Algorithm 1 is unchanged; the new model evaluations do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 adds HumanEval coding evaluation alongside the five existing datasets. Spider and MT-Bench were already evaluated, while ChatGPT-Prompts, ChatAlpaca, and CNN/DailyMail remain in Appendix C; their relocation is not lost coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds MCSS and typical decoding to the four existing speculative baselines in Table 5. Its downstream comparison also includes BiLD, Spectr, and SpecInfer, whereas v2 Table 6 compared downstream performance only against vanilla speculative decoding. SpD is the renamed existing speculative baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluations with Llama-3.1-8B targets and Llama-3.2-1B drafts, including Instruct variants, a four-token MTJD comparison, and HumanEval pass@1. Appendix F changes the stated default top-k from 20 to 10 while retaining top-p=0.9. This reported setting change does not establish that the retained Llama-2/OPT experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds acceptance-length measurements across thresholds for Llama-3 variants (Table 10), broader perplexity–quality analysis (Figure 4), and grouped energy–speed analysis (Figure 5). Existing beam-count, threshold, top-k/top-p, and fine-tuning analyses remain, mostly relocated within Appendix C.

E5.justification: v3 removes v2's explicit four-run description and the explanation that MT-Bench standard deviations also include task variation. Legacy uncertainty values remain in the appendices, but new main Tables 4–5 provide point estimates without run counts or uncertainty. The PDFs do not establish a reduction in actual repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 4–5 add substantial MTJD and MTAD results under new model settings; for example, Table 5 reports HumanEval pass@1 of 38.4 for MTAD versus 32.9 for SpD with Llama-3-Instruct. Table 10 adds threshold-dependent acceptance lengths. Matched older benchmark and ablation values are retained, so these additions are not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The MTJD definition, perplexity and approximation bounds, energy decomposition, and Appendix A proofs are retained. Equation 2's rewritten summation indexing and Equation 5's formatting do not substantively change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary replace the headline 21.2% perplexity reduction with a 25% downstream-performance improvement. The central joint-decoding, bounded-approximation, and energy-efficiency contributions remain, as do the reported 1.42× speedup and 1.54× energy-reduction headlines.

C2.justification: v3 explains why lossless methods can generate different sequences even with a fixed seed and acknowledges energy variation across L40 machine nodes (Section 5.2 and Appendix C.8). It removes the earlier explanation of good perplexity at threshold zero. Most existing mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes v2 Table 13's selected hyperparameters for each method/model/dataset and Appendix E's matched-input rule for perplexity evaluation. It instead supplies MTAD search ranges, explicitly reports temperature 1, and adds node-matching and licensing information. The reported code link changes from an anonymous repository to the named MTAD repository. Losing exact selected configurations materially reduces reproducibility detail.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for HumanEval, Llama-3, and MCSS, and briefly positions MCSS as extending SpecInfer through sampling without replacement in Section 6. The broader positioning against single-token decoding and alongside complementary draft-model improvements remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Prose is edited throughout the abstract, preliminaries, methodology, and energy discussion. Section 5 is reorganized around separate MTJD and MTAD evaluations, while the original benchmark discussion and ablations move into a reorganized Appendix C. Terminology, affiliations, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v3 introduces main Tables 4–5, supplementary Table 10, and Figures 4–5; relocates v2 Tables 4–7 and Figure 3 into the appendices; and removes the selected-hyperparameter table. Retained displays are resized or reformatted, and the document adopts an ICLR conference layout. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 Tables 4–5 extend direct MTJD quality tests and broaden MTAD's downstream comparisons beyond v2's SpD-only comparison, strengthening empirical support for the central quality claim. Gains are tempered by deleted run-count and selected-configuration information and missing uncertainty for new main results. Numerical reporting also needs correction: Table 5 implies approximately 7.2% mean relative speed improvement over MCSS, versus the 17.2% claimed in Section 5.2.
